questions.question: 没有老板要求，一位职员周末主动学新技能、回工作邮件，还把这称为「投资自己」。按韩炳哲《倦怠社会》的框架，该怎么看这件事？
options: 这仍是福柯式的规训：老板通过绩效考核在背后监视他，只是他自己没有察觉到这一点
这是免疫学范式下的病：外来的工作要求像病毒一样闯入私人时间，突破了身心的防线
这说明规训社会已经结束，人摆脱了外部禁令和监视，终于获得了可以自我实现的真正自主
这是自我剥削：「应该」内化成了「我能够」，带着自由感，更高效也无从反抗
questions.explanation: 韩炳哲认为功绩社会里「能够」并没有废掉「应该」，而是吞下了它：规训被装进了自己，剥削者和被剥削者合为一体。因为带着自由的感觉，自我剥削零监督成本，也没有可以反抗的对象。说他摆脱了强制、获得了自主，正是韩炳哲要拆穿的那种感受：你感到最自由的时候，恰恰是被管理得最彻底的时候。
questions.question_en: With no boss asking, an employee spends weekends learning new skills and answering work email, calling it "investing in myself." How would Byung-Chul Han's The Burnout Society read this?
options_en: As Foucauldian discipline as usual: the boss is watching through performance reviews, and the employee simply hasn't noticed
As a disease of the immunological paradigm: outside work demands invade private time like a virus and break through the body's defenses
As proof the disciplinary society is over: freed from external prohibitions and surveillance, the person has finally gained real autonomy for self-realization
As auto-exploitation: "should" has been internalized as "I can," and because it feels like freedom it is more efficient than outside exploitation and leaves nothing to resist
questions.explanation_en: For Han, "can" in the achievement society doesn't abolish "should" but swallows it: discipline is installed inside the self, and exploiter and exploited become one person. Because it feels like freedom, auto-exploitation needs no supervision and offers no one to rebel against. Reading it as hard-won autonomy is exactly the feeling Han sets out to expose: you are most thoroughly managed precisely when you feel most free.

questions.question: 韩炳哲说二十一世纪的典型疾病（抑郁、倦怠、注意缺陷等）不再是「免疫学」的，而是「神经元」的。这个区分的核心意思是什么？
options: 病因不是闯入的他者，而是同者过剩：刺激、选项、自我要求太多，没有敌人可抵抗
全球化让外来威胁变得更隐蔽、更难识别，免疫系统式的防御因此一再失灵、反应总是慢一步
规训社会的禁令和监视越积越多，人被压抑到极限，最终在神经层面崩溃，表现为抑郁和倦怠
社会压力已经能通过神经递质直接作用于大脑，所以这些病应当从生理层面而不是社会层面理解
questions.explanation: 免疫学范式靠「自己与非己」的二分对付外来者；韩炳哲认为新的暴力来自「肯定性」的过剩，压垮人的往往是一大堆都「挺好」的东西，就像身体不会对过量的糖产生免疫反应。说病因是禁令越积越多，就把他的诊断弄反了：他恰恰认为否定性的禁令已让位给没有边界的「能够」。
questions.question_en: Han says the signature illnesses of the 21st century (depression, burnout, attention disorders) are no longer "immunological" but "neuronal." What is the core of that distinction?
options_en: The cause is no longer an invading Other but an excess of the Same: too many stimuli, options and self-demands, with no identifiable enemy to fight
Globalization has made outside threats stealthier and harder to detect, so immune-style defenses keep failing and always react a step too late
The prohibitions and surveillance of disciplinary society keep piling up until people, repressed to the limit, break down neurologically
Social pressure now acts on the brain directly through neurotransmitters, so these illnesses should be understood physiologically rather than socially
questions.explanation_en: The immunological paradigm deals with outsiders through a self/non-self split. Han argues the new violence comes from an excess of positivity: what crushes people is often a pile of things that are each "fine," just as the body mounts no immune response to too much sugar. Blaming piled-up prohibitions gets his diagnosis backwards, since he holds that negative prohibition has given way to a boundless "can."

questions.question: 韩炳哲借汉德克区分了两种疲倦，并把出路指向「不做」。下面哪种休息最接近他珍视的那种？
options: 严格执行工作与生活的平衡，把运动、冥想和陪伴家人都写进日程，按时完成
一个不为产出的安息日：松开紧抓，自我变小，重新看见孩子、树叶和身边的人
安排一次高质量的度假，彻底给自己充满电，好让下周回去的工作效率明显回升
独自缩回自己的世界，关掉手机，不跟任何人说话，一直待到精力慢慢恢复为止
questions.explanation: 汉德克所说「信任世界的疲倦」是消极能力的疲倦：不再追逐，于是有了空间和别人一起「在」，韩炳哲把它和不为下周更高产而休息的安息日相连。充电和工作生活平衡仍是为了更有效地工作，充电的比喻本身就把人当成了电池；缩回自己、与人隔绝，则是功绩社会那种让人分裂的疲倦。
questions.question_en: Drawing on Peter Handke, Han distinguishes two kinds of tiredness and points to "not-doing" as a way out. Which kind of rest comes closest to what he values?
options_en: Strict work-life balance, with exercise, meditation and family time all scheduled into the calendar and checked off on time
A Sabbath with no output in view: letting go, the self shrinking, seeing the children, the leaves and the people nearby again
A carefully planned high-quality vacation that fully recharges you, so your productivity is noticeably higher when you return
Withdrawing into yourself, phone off, speaking to no one, and staying that way until your energy slowly comes back
questions.explanation_en: Handke's "tiredness that trusts the world" is the tiredness of negative potency: no longer chasing, you finally have room to simply be with others, and Han links it to a Sabbath that is not rest for the sake of next week's output. Recharging and work-life balance still serve more efficient work, and the recharging metaphor treats people as batteries. Withdrawing and cutting yourself off is the divisive tiredness of the achievement society.
